raw_response:
I will keep to the crop pattern I trust most here in Quzhou County: winter wheat followed by summer maize. That is what fits my land, my age, and the way I know how to farm. I do not want to take big risks on unfamiliar cash crops that need more market judgment or more hand labor. Wheat and maize are steady, easy to arrange with local seed, fertilizer, machines, and irrigation, and I understand their timing well. I will use improved seed instead of expensive high-risk options, put most of my fertilizer on as base plus topdressing, irrigate enough to protect yield but not waste water, and keep pesticide use limited to the main disease and insect pressure. I will plough before wheat to set the field up well, then use rotary tillage after wheat harvest so I can sow maize fast and keep the season on time.
